intended_object: The underlying scheme of the group scheme μ_n of n-th roots of unity over Spec K. It is the affine scheme Spec K[T]/(T^n − 1) ≅ Spec K[ℤ/nℤ], viewed as a scheme over Spec K. This comes from the docstring, the module documentation (Milne, Algebraic Groups 2.4) and how the file uses it.
explanation:
The definition takes Spec of the group algebra `AddMonoidAlgebra K (ZMod n)` = K[ℤ/nℤ] and regards it as an object of `Over (Spec K)` via the structure map given by `algebraMap`.

For n > 0, K[ℤ/nℤ] ≅ K[T]/(T^n − 1), so this is exactly the scheme underlying μ_n. The file proves this equivalence (`rootsOfUnityCoordinateAlgEquiv`). It also identifies the points of the scheme with the n-th roots of unity, and shows that the scheme is the kernel of the n-th power map on G_m.

For n = 0, ZMod 0 = ℤ, so the definition gives G_m = Spec K[T, T⁻¹]. That is the natural extension: every unit satisfies x^0 = 1. The module documentation states this extension openly, and it is harmless.

The base is an arbitrary commutative ring K, which is the standard generality for μ_n over an affine base. Mathlib has no roots-of-unity group scheme. It only has the general machinery for affine Hopf-algebra Spec, which this definition uses. So the definition is not too narrow, and it matches the intended object.
